# Exampleton Court Convicts Shell-Company Operator in Laundering Case

By Test Reporter · 9 June 2026

A court in Exampleton on Monday convicted the operator of a network of shell companies of
laundering the proceeds of an investment fraud, closing a case that investigators described as
a textbook layering scheme. The defendant, Notareal Persona, had pleaded not guilty.

Prosecutors said Persona registered eleven companies in three jurisdictions and moved client
deposits between their accounts in amounts just below reporting thresholds. The funds were then
converted into precious metals through a dealer that Persona also controlled.

According to the judgment, more than 4.2 million in invented currency units passed through
the network over two years. Banking staff had flagged the round-figure transfers repeatedly,
the court heard, but the alerts were closed without escalation.

The presiding judge said the scheme exploited the gap between institutions, with no single
bank seeing the full pattern. Persona was sentenced to four years and ordered to forfeit the
remaining balances held by the shell companies.

A spokesperson for the fictional banking supervisor said the case showed why beneficial
ownership registers matter for detecting layered structures earlier.
